solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Look! Game includes new monster's lair

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look! or behold

indicators.note: the game's letters take the next piece inside them, as if including it

parts.note: chess is a board game

explanation.surface: An excited cry: look, a game is set up that leads us to the monster's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look!' reads as an exclamation in the surface but is the archaic word for behold.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish lake is famously the supposed home of Nessie, its legendary monster.

clue.text: Suddenly attack ruffian hugging tree

indicators.note: the ruffian wraps around the tree, so one word's letters enclose the other's

parts.note: a lout is a rough, uncouth man
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: A thug clinging to a tree suddenly turns violent.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash out is the idiom for striking or attacking someone abruptly.

clue.text: Mark to pause, initially carrying bullets northwards

indicators.note: initially tells us to take only the opening letter of the word carrying
in a down clue going northwards means reading upwards, so the word for bullets runs backwards

parts.note: ammo is short for ammunition, such as bullets

explanation.surface: A punctuation note about pausing, then someone heading north with bullets.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'northwards' means read upwards, so the ammunition word gives OMMA.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation symbol signals a short break when reading a sentence.

clue.text: Modern England, few changes

indicators.note: changes says the letters of England and few are rearranged

explanation.surface: A comment that the country of England has changed little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges ENGLAND plus FEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Newfangled describes something novel and recent, usually said with mild disapproval of the up-to-date.

clue.text: Spiritual healer's bogus article

parts.note: sham means fake or bogus
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: The suggestion that a faith healer's item is fake.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after healer is read as 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a figure in many traditional cultures who heals through contact with spirits.

clue.text: Hairstyle for every mother's head

parts.note: per means for each or for every, as in miles per hour

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of mother's

explanation.surface: A hairdo for each mum's head of hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' takes M from 'mother's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A perm is a permanent wave, a chemically set curly hairdo.

clue.text: Grenade is being tossed — get ready!

indicators.note: tossed means thrown about, so the letters of grenade are jumbled

explanation.surface: A warning shout as a grenade is thrown: brace yourself!
explanation.walkthrough: 'is being tossed' rearranges GRENADE.
explanation.definitionFit: En garde is the fencer's call warning the opponent to take a guard position and be prepared.

clue.text: Face extremely greasy — it's humid

parts.note: mug is slang for the face

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters, of greasy

explanation.surface: Someone's face is very oily because the weather is so close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives GY, the ends of 'greasy'; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Muggy weather is warm, damp and oppressive, which is what humid air feels like.

clue.text: Thomas, we messed up a bit

indicators.note: messed up means disordered, so the letters of Thomas and we are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone admits to Thomas that they slightly bungled things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messed up' rearranges THOMAS plus WE.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhat is an adverb meaning to some extent, like the phrase a bit in 'a bit tired'.

clue.text: Excited in the past by golf

parts.note: ago means at a time in the past
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone recalls once being thrilled by a game of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means eagerly expectant, wide-eyed with excitement.

clue.text: Neighbourhoods beset by crime in global region

indicators.note: beset means surrounded, so the neighbourhoods are enclosed by the crime word

parts.note: theft is a crime
areas are districts or neighbourhoods

explanation.surface: Districts plagued by lawbreaking somewhere in a part of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The countries of eastern Asia, such as China and Japan, form a broad part of the world.

clue.text: Leader of Samurai in tree by a Japanese city

indicators.note: in places the leading letter inside the tree word

parts.note: the oak is a tree

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Samurai

explanation.surface: A chief warrior stationed in a tree beside a Japanese city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts S inside OAK, then A follows; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major port and commercial centre in Japan.

clue.text: Smoker's accessory lost around hotel

indicators.note: around has the word for lost go round the hotel letter

parts.note: astray means off course or lost
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A smoker's item has gone missing somewhere in a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts H inside ASTRAY.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashtray is the dish a smoker uses for ash and stubs.

clue.text: Also carrying suitcase for island

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the word for also holds the suitcase word inside

parts.note: too means also
a bag is a piece of luggage such as a suitcase

explanation.surface: A traveller to an island also has a suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is the smaller island of the Caribbean nation Trinidad and Tobago.

clue.text: Tested for counterfeit currency? Not this one!

definitions.text: Tested for counterfeit currency? Not this one!

parts.words: Tested for counterfeit currency? Not this one!
parts.note: people once bit a coin to test whether it was real metal; this digital money has no physical form to bite

explanation.surface: A wry remark about checking money for forgery.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as BIT COIN: the old test of biting a coin, which cannot be done to a purely digital currency.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a cryptocurrency, money existing only electronically, so no one can sink their teeth into it.

clue.text: River travellers not starting dessert

indicators.note: not starting means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: rafters travel down rivers on rafts

explanation.surface: People rafting downriver haven't yet begun their pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starting' drops R from RAFTERS. AFTERS is British informal for the dessert course.
explanation.definitionFit: Afters is British slang for the sweet course, the one that comes after the main meal.

clue.text: Hide Theseus and Ariadne, ultimately, above minotaur's home

indicators.note: in a down entry, above places the first pieces higher, so they come first
ultimately points to the final letter of each of Theseus and Ariadne

parts.note: in Greek myth the Minotaur lived in the labyrinth on Crete

explanation.surface: A mythological scene: the hero and princess hide over the monster's island lair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes S and E; 'above' sets them before CRETE.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete is to conceal or stash away, a less common sense than discharging a fluid.

clue.text: In addition, charity produces sacred songs

parts.note: PS, postscript, is something added at the end of a letter
alms are charitable gifts to the poor

explanation.surface: Moreover, a charity puts out religious music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produces' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalms are the hymns of the biblical Book of Psalms, sung in worship.

clue.text: Idiotic lists we developed

indicators.note: developed means worked into a new form, so the letters of lists and we are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses the lists they drew up as stupid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges LISTS plus WE.
explanation.definitionFit: Witless means lacking wits, foolish or silly.

clue.text: Liszt lawsuit holds back piece of music

indicators.note: back means the held letters read in reverse order
holds says the answer sits inside the run of letters of Liszt lawsuit

explanation.surface: A legal action involving the composer Liszt is holding up a musical work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' finds ZTLAW across 'Liszt lawsuit'; 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A waltz is a dance tune in triple time, a common kind of musical composition.

clue.text: Procure license to conceal artifact

indicators.note: to conceal says the answer is tucked away inside the words Procure license

explanation.surface: Getting a permit to hide an ancient object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to conceal' hides the answer in procuRE LICense.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object surviving from the past, an artifact of historic interest.

clue.text: Ladies and gents beginning to exercise for free

parts.note: in Britain Ladies and Gents are public toilets, and loo is slang for a toilet

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of exercise

explanation.surface: Use of the public toilets before exercising costs nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' takes E from 'exercise'. LOO is British slang for toilet; Ladies and Gents label public toilets.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose means unrestrained or at liberty, as in free.

clue.text: Spoils instrument in retrospect

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking back, so the word for instrument reads backwards

parts.note: a tool is an implement or instrument

explanation.surface: Looking back, a device is ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retrospect' reverses TOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Loot is plunder, the spoils taken in war or theft; Spoils is a noun here, not a verb.

clue.text: By oneself, holding hat for gangster

indicators.note: holding means the solo word grips the hat word inside it

parts.note: alone means by oneself
a cap is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: A mobster standing solo clutching his hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago mob boss of the Prohibition era.

clue.text: Metal unknown in Canada, at first

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of Canada

explanation.surface: A metal not found in Canada, at least initially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes C from 'Canada'.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinc is a bluish-white metallic chemical element.

clue.text: Sweatier when swimming, so to speak

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters of Sweatier moving about freely into a new order

explanation.surface: A swimmer grows more sweaty, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when swimming' rearranges SWEATIER.
explanation.definitionFit: As it were is an idiom that softens a figurative expression, the same as so to speak.
